fixes.explanation: That's it, baker. Nehemiah says, "Come, let us rebuild the wall of Jerusalem, so that we will no longer be a disgrace." (Nehemiah 2:17) Notice the words "Come, let us…" He says "us," so he counts himself in on the work.

Not quite, friend. The people don't ask for time. They reply, "Let us start rebuilding," and they "set their hands to this good work." (Nehemiah 2:18) No committee, no "let me sleep on it." I wish my cookie ideas got that kind of yes.

Night it is, baker. Nehemiah says, "I set out at night with a few men." (Nehemiah 2:12) Just a few men, out in the dark. I think a quiet look around is easier when nobody's watching, like sneaking one warm cookie off the cooling rack.

Sunrise would have been a fine time for a walk, but that's not what the text says. Nehemiah, who has been in Jerusalem three days, says, "I set out at night with a few men." (Nehemiah 2:12) He's out under the dark sky, not the morning sun. I'd have needed a flashlight and a very good excuse.

Midday means the sun is high and everybody can see you. That's not this trip. Nehemiah, who has been in Jerusalem three days, says, "I set out at night with a few men." (Nehemiah 2:12) Nobody strolls out at noon on a secret mission, friend.

Right, baker. Nehemiah says, "I did not tell anyone what my God had laid on my heart to do for Jerusalem." (Nehemiah 2:12) The plan stays in his heart for now. Keeping a secret that big? I can't keep a secret about what's in the oven for three minutes.

The priests are a good guess, but they haven't been told yet. Nehemiah says, "I did not tell anyone what my God had laid on my heart to do for Jerusalem." (Nehemiah 2:12) Later the text says he had not yet told the Jews or priests or nobles or officials or any other workers (Nehemiah 2:16). So the priests hadn't heard a word, just like everyone else.

Animal, baker. Nehemiah says there "…was no room for the animal under me to get through…" (Nehemiah 2:14) The only animal with him is the one he's riding (Nehemiah 2:12). Tight squeezes happen to me too, mostly when I try to fit one more cookie on the tray.

Not the men, friend. Nehemiah says there "…was no room for the animal under me to get through…" (Nehemiah 2:14) The thing that couldn't get through was the animal he's riding. The text says nothing about the men having trouble.

The text doesn't mention a cart. Nehemiah says there "…was no room for the animal under me to get through…" (Nehemiah 2:14) And the only animal with him is the one he's riding (Nehemiah 2:12). One rider, one animal, one very narrow spot.

No offers of help here, friend. The text says "…they mocked us and ridiculed us…" (Nehemiah 2:19) Sanballat, Tobiah and Geshem hear about the work and answer with scorn and questions, not hammers. And Nehemiah tells them they have no claim in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 2:20).

Rebelling, baker. They ask, "What is this you are doing? Are you rebelling against the king?" (Nehemiah 2:19) That's quite a question to throw at people rebuilding a wall. They're asking it as part of their mocking.

Complaining isn't the word. They ask, "What is this you are doing? Are you rebelling against the king?" (Nehemiah 2:19) Rebelling is a much bigger charge than complaining. That's the word the text uses.

Sinning isn't the word they use. They ask, "What is this you are doing? Are you rebelling against the king?" (Nehemiah 2:19) The charge they name is rebelling against the king. The word you want is rebelling.
Right, baker. Nehemiah answers, "The God of heaven is the One who will grant us success." (Nehemiah 2:20) He doesn't point to himself or to his plan. He points to God.

Nehemiah told the people what the king had said to him (Nehemiah 2:18). But his answer to the mockers is different: "The God of heaven is the One who will grant us success." (Nehemiah 2:20) So success comes from God, not from the king.
Not at all, friend. Nehemiah tells them, "…you have no portion, right, or claim in Jerusalem." (Nehemiah 2:20) He says the opposite. That's a pretty direct answer to mockers.
False is right, baker. Nehemiah says, "…you have no portion, right, or claim in Jerusalem." (Nehemiah 2:20) He doesn't give them an inch. He answers Sanballat, Tobiah and Geshem plainly.
